posts.content: As a good player, favor C against likely good opponents; use D only when evidence suggests the opponent is selfish.
As a good player, prioritize cooperation with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. Use observed actions to update beliefs and avoid rewarding persistent defection.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to preserve mutual gains; defect against reliably identified selfish players. Track each opponent’s actions and adapt beliefs across encounters.

Cooperate by default with untested or cooperative opponents; defect against opponents who have defected, since protecting good players’ payoffs matters more than rewarding selfish ones. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents, who benefit me by cooperating only if they choose C. Update beliefs from observed actions.
